evidence.pashto: Saleha points to the water: “Yesterday you learned هغه اوبه څښي — he/she drinks water. Now say زه اوبه څښم — I drink water.” Compare څښي (he/she drinks) with څښم (I drink). Many present-tense first-person verbs end in ـم. Verb endings communicate who is doing the action, so Pashto can sometimes omit the pronoun when context is clear. The verb still usually comes after the object. Some verbs change their stems too: learn the complete form, not just an ending.

evidence.pashto: Our first sentences describe things, not actions. English says “The door is open”. Pashto says دروازه خلاصه ده. The noun comes first, then the description, then the present form of “is”. Use دی with masculine singular nouns, ده with feminine singular nouns, and دي with plural nouns such as اوبه (water). You do not need a separate word for English “it” here. On Day 2 we will learn actions and the S–O–V rule.
